decisions.executionNote: Use left arm for the left basket; raise and gradually tilt toward a top-down approach, keeping the right arm parked.
Advance above the back egg while completing most of the downward wrist tilt. Maintain smooth elbow-up motion.
Align the open fingers over the back egg and lower cautiously; wrist view will refine the final grasp height.
Refine the back-egg alignment from wrist RGB, moving slightly forward and left while descending with open fingers.
Center on the visible egg, close fully, and make a short vertical test lift; retention must be checked visually.
Egg appears retained between the fingers. Lift clear of the basket and start toward the holder with the gripper commanded closed.
Carry the retained egg above the holder's back-left cup. Keep the left link on its side of center and the right arm stationary.
Lower toward the back-left cup and make a small rightward alignment correction using the head view. Keep the egg closed in the fingers.
Egg is visible at the back-left cup and the wrist may be contacting the lid. Open and withdraw upward-left to clear the holder and inspect placement.
First egg is visibly seated in the back-left cup. Return open to the basket's back-right egg, restoring the nearly vertical grasp.
Descend open around the basket's back-right egg, using the previous grasp height as a guide and checking alignment before closing.
Close on the centered second egg and lift vertically for a visual retention check, avoiding the basket rim.
Second egg is visibly retained. Carry it above the empty front-left cup, keeping the left wrist to the left of center.
Lower the second egg toward the front-left cup with a small rightward correction; retain the egg until it is close to the cup bottom.
Second egg is visible in the front-left cup. Open and withdraw from the holder, then return above the two remaining eggs.
Approach the basket's front-left remaining egg with open fingers, lowering only after moving above it.
Make a small centering correction, close on the third egg, and lift vertically to check retention.
The third egg was not retained and shifted left. Reopen, recenter over its new position, and descend further before retrying.
The egg moved inward and the left finger appears near the rim. Shift inward and straighten the approach before a shallow descent.
Recenter slightly left on the third egg, close, and test a short lift. Check retention before transporting.
Retention remains uncertain: the egg sits near the finger tips. Reopen and approach slightly farther forward and deeper around its body.
The fingers now surround the egg body. Make a slight backward centering correction, close fully, and lift to verify this retry.
Third egg is now visibly retained. Lift clear and begin carrying toward the remaining right-side cups, keeping the left wrist on its side of center.
Move the retained third egg above the back-right cup, tilting the tool so the left wrist remains left of center while the egg reaches the cup.
Lower the third egg toward the back-right cup, making a small rightward tool correction while keeping the wrist left of center.
The wrist is near the lid and the egg appears too far right. Back off slightly and shift left over the cup before release.
The third egg fell onto the right-side table. Open and clear the left wrist from the lid; prepare the right arm to recover the egg without crossing arms.
Replan after the continuity rejection: slide the open left tool back-left in small increments to unhook it from the lid, while raising and tilting the right tool toward the fallen egg.
Left tool remains caught near the lid. Narrow the empty fingers and withdraw backward before further lateral motion. Continue right-arm alignment over the loose egg.
Bridge toward the last accepted wrist orientation to satisfy continuity, then narrow and retract the empty left fingers. Right approach remains slow.
Try a primarily vertical left-tool clearance with open fingers, bridging tracking residuals gently. Lower the right tool toward the loose egg with a vertical grasp.
Left tool is now clear; retreat it over the basket. Center and lower the open right fingers around the loose egg on the table.
Refine and close the right grasp on the table egg, then test lift. Align the left arm above the last basket egg. The lid has fallen closed and will need reopening before placement.
Right egg is retained; hold it clear to the right. Use the free left hand to approach the closed lid's front edge for reopening before further placement.
Align the left fingers across the lid's front edge while keeping the right egg held clear. Approach cautiously to inspect possible purchase on the lip.
Try to pinch the lid's front lip with the left fingers, moving slowly inward and down; right hand continues holding the recovered egg.
Test whether the left fingers have purchase on the lid lip by lifting and following its opening arc. Keep the right egg stationary and closed.
The lid was not grasped. Reposition the left hand in front of the holder and rotate to pinch its lip horizontally, while the right hand retains the egg.
Use smaller increments after the IK rejection to retreat and rotate the left wrist without changing elbow configuration.
Continue moving the left hand in front of the holder and toward a horizontal lip-grasp orientation, with gradual joint-continuous motion.
After the continuity interruption, use smaller wrist rotations and lower in front of the lid, aiming the fingers along its front lip.
Pinch the front-left lid lip from the nearly horizontal approach, then make a short upward test pull while the right arm holds the egg clear.
The lid has lifted slightly. Continue supporting its front lip, moving upward and toward the hinge with a gradual upward wrist rotation.
Continue lifting the lid lip with much smaller increments after the wrist continuity rejection. Keep the recovered egg held safely to the right.
Lid is visibly open. Withdraw the left tool downstage-left and bring the retained right egg above the right-side cups, keeping the arms separated.
The right egg slipped onto the table during transport. Reopen and approach its new position for a deeper grasp; retreat and restore the left wrist away from the holder.
Move the right fingers backward and lower around the table egg's equator for a deeper grasp. Continue restoring the left wrist in free space.
Recenter the right fingers slightly backward-left, close, and test lift. Restore the left hand toward a vertical approach over the basket without crossing.
The recovered egg is now deeply between the right fingers. Lift gently while the open left hand approaches the final basket egg.
Lower the left fingers deeper around the last basket egg. Carry the right egg slowly toward the front-right cup, watching for slip.
Right egg slipped again; reopen for a deeper, slower recovery. Center the left egg between the fingers, close, and test a very small lift.
Lift the left egg gently to verify retention. Recenter the right fingers on the loose egg's shifted position and lower around its body before closing.
Close the right fingers around the centered egg and lift slowly. Keep the left egg retained and raise it clear of the basket.
Both eggs appear retained. Hold the left egg still and lift the right one slowly with minimal lateral acceleration before crossing the holder rim.
Carry the right egg very slowly toward the front-right cup with a gradual velocity ramp; keep the left egg stationary.
The slow transfer is retaining the egg. Continue gently above the front-right cup before descending; left egg remains held still.
Center the retained right egg over the front-right cup, then lower gradually toward the cup bottom while keeping the left egg stationary.
Set the right egg into the front-right cup, open fully, and lift straight up to check that it remains seated.
Three eggs are visibly seated. Clear the right arm and slowly lift and tilt the final left-held egg forward-right so the wrist can stay left and away from the lid.
Continue the slow final-egg transfer while establishing a forward-right reach angle. Park the empty right hand farther right to leave a clear approach.
Carry the final egg slowly toward the empty back-right cup, retaining the forward-reaching wrist angle and keeping the right arm parked.
Continue the gentle final-egg approach, lowering slightly while still above the holder and maintaining the secure closed grasp.
Align the final egg with the empty back-right cup and lower slowly, with a small backward correction to stay away from the upright lid.
Make the final small alignment and lower the egg into the back-right cup, then open without sweeping across the neighboring eggs.
Withdraw the open left fingers upward and back-left so the final egg can settle, then inspect all four cups before closing the lid.
All four eggs are visibly seated. Begin returning the left arm while bringing the closed right fingers toward the back of the upright lid for a gentle closing push.
Position the closed right fingers just above and behind the lid's top edge. Continue withdrawing the left arm toward its origin.
Gently contact the back of the lid's top edge with the closed right fingers and push toward closure; finish restoring the left wrist near origin.
Follow the lid edge toward the front and downward with a gentle closing sweep, monitoring contact. Settle the left arm at its starting pose.
Lid remains upright; the previous sweep was in front of it. Reposition the closed right fingers higher and behind its top edge before pushing forward.
Lower the closed fingertips just behind the upright lid's top edge to establish contact before the closing sweep.
Contact appears established at the lid edge. Push gently toward the front, following the initial downward closing arc.
The lid is beginning to rotate closed. Follow it forward and downward with the closed fingertips while keeping the left arm at origin.
Continue following the lid's closing arc rather than pressing straight down, with small pose corrections to account for contact deflection.
